category: Configuration keys, self-hosting and export server
description: Keys of the JSON configuration object (Extras > Configuration, DRAWIO_CONFIG, the configure embed action or the Confluence/Jira admin page) that customise fonts, colours, libraries, default styles, menus, templates, grid and editor behaviour, followed by the environment variables and endpoints of the self-hosted jgraph/drawio Docker image and the server-side image export service.

tools.name: defaultFonts (configuration key)
tools.description: Array that replaces the list of font families offered in the Format panel's font dropdown. Entries are plain family names or objects {fontFamily, fontUrl} for web fonts, in which case the URL is stored with the cell (fontSource) so exports can embed the font. Set it to expose corporate fonts to every user of an installation.

parameters.name: string
parameters.description: Font family name available on viewers' machines.

parameters.name: {fontFamily, fontUrl}
parameters.description: Web font entry; fontUrl is a CSS or font file URL.

tools.example: {"defaultFonts": ["Helvetica", "Verdana", "Times New Roman", "Garamond", "Comic Sans MS", "Courier New", "Georgia", "Lucida Console", "Tahoma"]}
tools.notes: customFonts prepends to the default list instead of replacing it; fontCss injects @font-face rules but does not add entries to the dropdown.

tools.name: customFonts / fontCss (configuration keys)
tools.description: customFonts is an array (same entry types as defaultFonts) added in front of the built-in font list, keeping the defaults available. fontCss is a string of CSS @font-face rules injected into the editor so a named family renders; it must be paired with an entry in defaultFonts/customFonts (or a fontUrl entry) to be selectable, and the font host must be allowed by the CSP.

parameters.name: customFonts
parameters.description: Array of names or {fontFamily, fontUrl} objects.

tools.notes: Fonts in PNG exports come from the rendering machine; SVG exports embed fonts when embedSvgFonts is true (default).

tools.name: presetColors / customPresetColors (configuration keys)
tools.description: presetColors replaces the upper palette of the colour dialog (the preset swatches) with an array of hex codes without #; customPresetColors prepends colours to the existing presets instead. Use them to put brand colours first for fill, line and font pickers.

parameters.name: presetColors
parameters.description: Array of RRGGBB strings replacing the presets.

parameters.name: customPresetColors
parameters.description: Array added before the built-in presets.

tools.notes: defaultColors controls the lower palette; colorNames adds tooltips to swatches.

tools.name: defaultColors (configuration key)
tools.description: Array of hex codes (no #) that replaces the lower palette of the colour dialog, the grid of standard colours shown under the presets. Combine with presetColors to fully control what users can pick with one click.
tools.notes: Users can still type any colour in the dialog's text field.

tools.name: defaultColorSchemes / customColorSchemes (configuration keys)
tools.description: Colour schemes are the one-click fill/stroke/font combinations shown at the top of the Style tab. defaultColorSchemes replaces the pages of schemes with an array of arrays of objects {fill, stroke, font, gradient}; customColorSchemes adds pages before the defaults. Each inner array is one page of the scheme picker.

parameters.name: fill / stroke / font / gradient
parameters.description: Colours of one scheme entry (hex with #, or none).

tools.notes: The first page also drives the colours used by the Sketch/Simple themes' quick style buttons.

tools.name: defaultVertexStyle / defaultEdgeStyle / defaultTextStyle (configuration keys)
tools.description: Initial default styles applied to new shapes, connectors and text: defaultVertexStyle and defaultEdgeStyle are objects of style key/value pairs merged into every inserted cell (users can still override them with Set as Default Style unless updateDefaultStyle is false), and defaultTextStyle is the style string for text elements. Use them to enforce fonts, rounded corners, edge routing or arrowheads across an organisation.

parameters.name: defaultVertexStyle
parameters.description: Object of style keys for vertices.

parameters.name: defaultEdgeStyle
parameters.description: Object of style keys for edges (built-in default: edgeStyle orthogonalEdgeStyle).

tools.notes: Values are strings. Sidebar shapes carry their own explicit styles, which take precedence over these defaults.

tools.name: defaultLibraries (configuration key)
tools.description: Semicolon-separated string of library keys shown in the sidebar for users who have not chosen their own set (built-in default general;uml;er;bpmn;flowchart;basic;arrows2). The order defines the order of palettes. Equivalent to the libs= URL parameter but persistent.

parameters.name: defaultLibraries
parameters.description: Keys from the More Shapes dialog separated by ;

tools.notes: Use override:true (or bump version) to apply it to users who already saved a library selection.

tools.name: libraries (configuration key, custom sidebar sections)
tools.description: Adds sections and libraries to the More Shapes dialog and the sidebar: an array of {title: {main, <lang>}, entries: [{id, title: {main}, desc: {main}, preview, libs: [{title: {main}, data: [...shapes...]} or {url}]}]}. Each library entry can inline shape definitions (data arrays with xml/w/h/title/aspect like an .xml library) or reference a library file by URL, so an organisation ships its stencils as part of the configuration.

parameters.name: title / desc
parameters.description: Objects keyed by language ('main' is the default).

parameters.name: entries[].id
parameters.description: Key usable in defaultLibraries and libs=.

parameters.name: libs[].url / libs[].data
parameters.description: External library file or inline shape array.

tools.example: Add {"defaultLibraries": "corp;general"} so the custom section appears first for everyone.
tools.notes: URLs must be reachable with CORS from the browser; the Docker image can host them under its webapp folder.

tools.name: enabledLibraries (configuration key)
tools.description: Array of library keys the More Shapes dialog offers; libraries not listed are hidden from the dialog and from shape search (null enables everything). Use it to restrict users to approved notations, e.g. only C4 and ArchiMate in an architecture-governance setup.

parameters.name: enabledLibraries
parameters.description: Array of keys, or null for all.

tools.notes: Existing diagrams that use other libraries still render; only the sidebar is restricted.

tools.name: defaultCustomLibraries / appendCustomLibraries / enableCustomLibraries (configuration keys)
tools.description: Custom-library handling: defaultCustomLibraries is an array of library ids to open automatically (same prefixes as clibs=, e.g. U<url>, G<drive id>), appendCustomLibraries:true places them after the built-in libraries instead of before, and enableCustomLibraries:false removes New Library / Open Library so users cannot add their own.
tools.notes: In embed mode custom libraries additionally require the libraries=1 URL parameter.

tools.name: css / customCss (configuration keys)
tools.description: Raw CSS injected into the editor page to restyle the UI (hide buttons, change panel colours, enlarge sidebar thumbnails, brand the toolbar). Use CSS selectors on draw.io's ge* classes (geMenubar, geSidebar, geFormat, geToolbar, geDiagramContainer). Diagram rendering itself is not affected.
tools.notes: Class names may change between versions; test after upgrades. hideMenus/hideMenuItems is the supported way to remove menu entries.

tools.name: ui, darkColor, defaultAdaptiveColors, enableLightDarkColors (configuration keys)
tools.description: Appearance defaults: ui selects the default theme for Confluence Cloud (kennedy, atlas, dark, min); darkColor (default #2A2A2A) is the dark-mode background and darkColorVar its CSS variable; defaultAdaptiveColors chooses how fixed colours adapt in dark mode (auto, simple or none; desktop defaults to simple); enableLightDarkColors:false stops the editor from using the CSS light-dark() function; defaultGridColor, defaultDarkGridColor, defaultPageBackgroundColor and defaultDarkPageBackgroundColor set grid and page colours per mode.

parameters.name: ui
parameters.description: kennedy | atlas | dark | min (Confluence Cloud default theme).

parameters.name: darkColor / darkColorVar
parameters.description: Dark background colour and CSS variable name.

parameters.name: defaultGridColor / defaultDarkGridColor / defaultPageBackgroundColor / defaultDarkPageBackgroundColor
parameters.description: Grid and page colours for light/dark mode.

tools.notes: For the web app the theme is chosen with the ui= URL parameter or Extras > Theme; the ui key applies to Confluence Cloud.

tools.name: hideMenus / hideMenuItems (configuration keys)
tools.description: hideMenus is an array of top-level menu names to remove (file, edit, view, arrange, extras, help) and hideMenuItems an array of action/menu-item ids to hide wherever they appear (e.g. plugins, configuration, editDiagram, exportVsdx, publishLink, share). Used by embedding hosts and locked-down installations to remove functions that bypass the host's storage or policies.
tools.notes: Keyboard shortcuts for hidden items may still work unless keyboardShortcuts is customised.

tools.name: keyboardShortcuts (configuration key)
tools.description: Array of custom key bindings that add to or replace the built-in shortcuts: each entry names an action id and a key combination (key code plus control/shift/alt flags), letting an installation map corporate conventions or free keys reserved by the embedding host (see also passThroughKeys, which lists chords forwarded to the host instead of being handled).

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Editor action id (e.g. undo, redo, fitWindow, toggleShapes).

parameters.name: passThroughKeys
parameters.description: Chords not intercepted by the editor (embed mode).

tools.notes: Key codes are JavaScript keyCode values (A=65 ... Z=90).

tools.name: templateFile / customTemplates / enabledTemplateSections (configuration keys)
tools.description: Templates dialog customisation: templateFile is the URL of an XML index describing template sections and files (the format of draw.io's own templates/index.xml) that replaces the built-in catalogue; customTemplates adds templates to existing sections; enabledTemplateSections restricts which sections are visible (null shows all). Use them to offer approved starting points for architecture or process diagrams.

parameters.name: templateFile
parameters.description: URL of the template index XML (<templates><template url=... section=... /></templates>).

parameters.name: customTemplates
parameters.description: Array of template definitions appended to sections.

parameters.name: enabledTemplateSections
parameters.description: Array of section ids or null.

tools.notes: Template files must be served with CORS. The Docker image can host them under /usr/local/tomcat/webapps/draw/templates/.

tools.name: globalVars (configuration key)
tools.description: Object of name/value pairs available to every diagram as %name% placeholders (after cell, ancestor and diagram attributes are checked). Useful for organisation-wide values such as company name, environment or documentation base URL, and for embedding hosts that inject user or page context.
tools.example: Label "%company% network" with placeholders enabled shows "ACME Corp network".
tools.notes: The vars= URL parameter provides the same per link; the embed configure action can set globalVars per session.

tools.name: gridSteps, defaultGridSize, defaultGridEnabled, gridColor keys (configuration keys)
tools.description: Grid defaults: defaultGridSize (px, default 10) for new diagrams, defaultGridEnabled (initial visibility), gridSteps (number of minor steps between major grid lines, default 4) and the colour keys defaultGridColor / defaultDarkGridColor. Diagrams store their own gridSize and grid attributes on mxGraphModel, so these only affect new files.
tools.notes: The pageFormat key sets the default paper size in the same spirit.

tools.name: styles (configuration key, Style tab presets)
tools.description: Array of colour objects shown in the Style tab when nothing is selected, i.e. the diagram-wide colour presets ({commonStyle: {fontColor, strokeColor, fillColor}, graph: {background, gridColor}, ...}). It lets an installation define whole-diagram looks (light, dark, brand) that users apply with one click.

parameters.name: graph
parameters.description: background and gridColor of the page.

tools.notes: Distinct from defaultVertexStyle: styles are applied on demand to existing cells.

tools.name: colorNames (configuration key)
tools.description: Object mapping colour codes (RRGGBB, upper case, no #) to display names shown as tooltips in the colour dialog and in the Format panel swatches, so brand palettes can be identified by name ('Primary blue') rather than hex value.
tools.notes: Names appear only for the exact codes listed.

tools.name: thumbWidth, thumbHeight, sidebarWidth, expandLibraries, sidebarTitles, shapePicker (configuration keys)
tools.description: Sidebar and picker layout: thumbWidth/thumbHeight (default 46 px) size the shape thumbnails, sidebarWidth sets the initial panel width in px, expandLibraries:false starts palettes collapsed, sidebarTitles:true shows titles under thumbnails (sidebarTitleSize sets the font size) and shapePicker is an object configuring the quick shape picker popup (the shapes offered when clicking a hover arrow or double-clicking the canvas).

parameters.name: sidebarTitles / sidebarTitleSize
parameters.description: Show titles and their size in pt.

parameters.name: shapePicker
parameters.description: Object describing the shape picker entries.

tools.notes: The URL parameter sidebar-entries=large is a per-session alternative for bigger thumbnails.

tools.name: emptyDiagramXml / emptyLibraryXml (configuration keys)
tools.description: XML used for a new blank diagram and for a new library. emptyDiagramXml can contain a preconfigured mxGraphModel (page size, grid, background, a title block or watermark cells) so every new file starts from the corporate frame; emptyLibraryXml (default <mxlibrary>[]</mxlibrary>) seeds new libraries.
tools.usage: {"emptyDiagramXml": "<mxGraphModel dx=\"0\" dy=\"0\" grid=\"1\" gridSize=\"10\" guides=\"1\" tooltips=\"1\" connect=\"1\" arrows=\"1\" fold=\"1\" page=\"1\" pageScale=\"1\" pageWidth=\"1169\" pageHeight=\"827\" math=\"0\" shadow=\"0\"><root><mxCell id=\"0\"/><mxCell id=\"1\" parent=\"0\"/></root></mxGraphModel>"}
tools.example: Set pageWidth/pageHeight to 1169 x 827 (A4 landscape) and grid="0" in emptyDiagramXml to change the default page for all users.
tools.notes: Templates chosen from the Templates dialog replace this XML.

tools.name: autosaveDelay, compressXml, compact (configuration keys)
tools.description: File-handling defaults: autosaveDelay is the pause in milliseconds after the last change before autosave runs (cloud storage and embed autosave events); compressXml:true writes deflate-compressed page content into .drawio files (default false in current versions, so files are plain XML); compact:true strips extra metadata (host, agent, etag) from the saved <mxfile> for cleaner diffs.

parameters.name: compressXml
parameters.description: true compresses diagram XML in files.

tools.notes: Extras > Compressed toggles compression per session; the CLI flag --uncompressed rewrites existing files.

tools.name: override, version, settingsName, showSplashOnStart (configuration keys)
tools.description: Deployment controls: override:true makes the configuration replace settings users have saved locally (otherwise user settings win); version is a string that, when changed, resets stored settings so a new configuration takes effect; settingsName chooses the local-storage key under which settings are stored (separate profiles per host page); showSplashOnStart controls whether the start screen appears when the app opens without a file.

parameters.name: override
parameters.description: true forces the configuration over local settings.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Change to trigger a settings reset.

tools.example: Roll out a new palette: update presetColors and bump version to "3" so every browser picks it up.
tools.notes: Extras > Configuration > Reset clears the stored configuration in the browser.

tools.name: simpleLabels, stopEditingOnEnter, zoomFactor, zoomWheel (configuration keys)
tools.description: Editing behaviour: simpleLabels:true disables word wrap and rich formatting for new labels (plain text cells), stopEditingOnEnter:true makes Enter finish label editing (Shift+Enter inserts a line break), zoomFactor (default 1.2) is the multiplier for each zoom step with the wheel or Ctrl +/-, and zoomWheel:true zooms with the plain mouse wheel instead of requiring Ctrl/Alt.
tools.notes: Related: pasteAtMousePointer, insertAnimations, intersectionSelect, enableSizeGuides and copyOnConnect tune other interaction details.

tools.name: maxImageSize, maxImageBytes, removeImageMetadata (configuration keys)
tools.description: Image insertion limits: maxImageSize (default 520 px) is the largest width or height at which an inserted image is placed (larger images are scaled down on the canvas, not re-encoded), maxImageBytes (default 1,000,000) is the maximum file size accepted for embedding as a data URI, and removeImageMetadata:true (default) strips EXIF/metadata from embedded images.

parameters.name: maxImageBytes
parameters.description: Max embedded image size in bytes.

tools.notes: Large embedded images bloat .drawio files; prefer linking images by URL in self-hosted setups with the proxy enabled.

tools.name: pageFormat, defaultPageVisible, defaultFileType (configuration keys)
tools.description: Document defaults: pageFormat {width, height} sets the paper size (in px at 100 %, e.g. 827 x 1169 for A4 portrait) of new diagrams, defaultPageVisible sets whether page view is on, and defaultFileType (drawio, png, svg or html) chooses the extension proposed by Save As, so teams that store .drawio.svg in Git can make it the default.
tools.notes: File > Page Setup changes the page format per diagram (mxGraphModel pageWidth/pageHeight).

tools.name: mermaid (configuration key)
tools.description: Default Mermaid configuration object passed to the Mermaid renderer used by Arrange > Insert > Advanced > Mermaid and by mermaid image shapes: theme (default, dark, forest, neutral), themeVariables, fontFamily, flowchart/sequence/gantt options and securityLevel. Lets an installation match Mermaid output to its colour scheme.
tools.notes: Per-diagram overrides can be given in the Mermaid source with %%{init: {...}}%%.

tools.name: lockdown, restrictExport, enableExportUrl (configuration keys)
tools.description: Data-protection switches: lockdown:true disables every transmission of diagram data except to the selected storage location (no image proxy, no PlantUML, no export server, no share links); restrictExport:true removes the export-to-other-format functions; enableExportUrl:false hides File > Export as > URL. Use them in regulated environments together with stealth=1.
tools.notes: The desktop app is offline by design and needs none of these.

tools.name: enableAi, aiModels, claudeApiKey / gptApiKey / geminiApiKey (AI configuration keys)
tools.description: Configuration of the AI diagram-generation features (Smart Template, generate from prompt): enableAi turns them on (default on in the online editor, off in Confluence and self-hosted unless configured), the *ApiKey keys hold provider credentials (claudeApiKey, gptApiKey, geminiApiKey; gptUrl for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and aiModels is an array of {name, model, config} entries offered in the model picker, with aiConfigs/aiActions/aiGlobals for advanced prompt and action definitions.

parameters.name: aiModels
parameters.description: Array of {name, model, config} shown to users.

tools.notes: Keys placed in DRAWIO_CONFIG are delivered to every browser; treat them as public or use a proxy endpoint via gptUrl. There is no DRAWIO_ENABLE_AI environment variable.

tools.name: Desktop preferences and settings storage (.drawio-config, AppData)
tools.description: The desktop app stores editor settings (recent files, theme, sidebar libraries, format panel state, the JSON from Extras > Configuration) in Electron local storage under the user profile: Windows %APPDATA%\draw.io\, macOS ~/Library/Application Support/draw.io, Linux ~/.config/draw.io. In the browser the same data lives in localStorage keys .drawio-config (settings) and .configuration (Extras > Configuration JSON). Deleting them resets the editor; Extras > Configuration > Reset does it from the UI.
tools.usage: Windows: C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\draw.io\   |   browser DevTools > Application > Local Storage > .drawio-config / .configuration

parameters.name: .configuration
parameters.description: Configuration JSON entered in Extras > Configuration.

tools.example: To deploy a shared configuration to desktop users, distribute the JSON and have them paste it into Extras > Configuration, or set it through the enterprise deployment tooling of your OS.
tools.notes: The desktop app also checks github.com for updates unless DRAWIO_DISABLE_UPDATE=true or --disable-update is used; --disable-acceleration turns off GPU acceleration.

tools.name: DRAWIO_SERVER_URL / DRAWIO_BASE_URL / DRAWIO_VIEWER_URL / DRAWIO_LIGHTBOX_URL / DRAWIO_LANG (Docker environment variables)
tools.description: URL settings of the jgraph/drawio container: DRAWIO_SERVER_URL is the public deployment URL with trailing slash (a sub-path also sets the Tomcat context path); DRAWIO_BASE_URL is the same without trailing slash for viewer/lightbox/embed code paths (derived automatically when only one is given); DRAWIO_VIEWER_URL points the HTML embed snippet at a hosted viewer.min.js; DRAWIO_LIGHTBOX_URL sets the lightbox base used by embeds; DRAWIO_LANG sets the default UI language when no lang= parameter or user choice exists.

parameters.name: DRAWIO_SERVER_URL
parameters.description: Public URL with trailing slash, e.g. https://www.example.com/drawio/.

parameters.name: DRAWIO_BASE_URL
parameters.description: Same URL without trailing slash (optional, backwards compatible).

tools.notes: The container must run with GID 0 or the entrypoint skips all runtime configuration. OAuth redirect URIs for Google/OneDrive/GitLab must be registered under DRAWIO_SERVER_URL.

tools.name: DRAWIO_CONFIG / DRAWIO_CONFIG_FILE (Docker environment variables)
tools.description: Server-side editor configuration for the Docker image: DRAWIO_CONFIG holds the configuration JSON object verbatim (written into window.DRAWIO_CONFIG, must be valid JSON, not a file path) and DRAWIO_CONFIG_FILE names a file inside the container containing the same JSON (bind mount or ConfigMap), taking precedence over DRAWIO_CONFIG. Every key from Extras > Configuration is accepted.
tools.usage:
docker run -p 8080:8080 -e DRAWIO_CONFIG='{"defaultFonts":["Helvetica"],"compressXml":false}' jgraph/drawio
docker run -p 8080:8080 -v ./drawio-config.json:/config/drawio-config.json:ro -e DRAWIO_CONFIG_FILE=/config/drawio-config.json jgraph/drawio

parameters.name: DRAWIO_CONFIG
parameters.description: Inline JSON (use compose map syntax, not list syntax, to avoid quote problems).

parameters.name: DRAWIO_CONFIG_FILE
parameters.description: Path to a JSON file in the container.

tools.notes: The entrypoint logs a warning when the value does not parse as JSON. Fonts must still be reachable over HTTP(S) by the browser.

tools.name: DRAWIO_CSP_HEADER / ENABLE_DRAWIO_PROXY / DRAWIO_USE_HTTP (Docker environment variables)
tools.description: Security settings of the container: DRAWIO_CSP_HEADER overrides the default Content-Security-Policy meta tag (start from the policy in docker-entrypoint.sh when allowing extra font or image hosts); ENABLE_DRAWIO_PROXY=1 enables the /proxy servlet so images from external URLs can be embedded and exported; DRAWIO_USE_HTTP=1 allows plain-HTTP deployments (insecure: OAuth tokens travel unencrypted).
tools.usage: docker run -e ENABLE_DRAWIO_PROXY=1 -e DRAWIO_CSP_HEADER="default-src 'self'; font-src *; img-src * data:; ..." jgraph/drawio
tools.example: ENABLE_DRAWIO_PROXY=1 lets Arrange > Insert > Image with an external URL render in PNG exports.
tools.notes: Without the proxy, external images render in the editor (if CORS allows) but may be missing from exports.

tools.name: DRAWIO_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / DRAWIO_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET / DRAWIO_GOOGLE_APP_ID (Docker environment variables)
tools.description: Enable Google Drive storage in a self-hosted instance with your own OAuth client: DRAWIO_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and DRAWIO_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET from the Google Cloud console and DRAWIO_GOOGLE_APP_ID (the numeric project number that prefixes the client id). Optional DRAWIO_GOOGLE_VIEWER_CLIENT_ID / _SECRET / _APP_ID configure separate read-only credentials for a viewer deployment. Unset means Google Drive is disabled.
tools.example: Register https://drawio.example.com/google as the OAuth redirect URI, then start the container with the three variables.
tools.notes: Sign-in under a sub-path needs image 31.5.2 or newer.

tools.name: DRAWIO_MSGRAPH_CLIENT_ID / DRAWIO_MSGRAPH_CLIENT_SECRET / DRAWIO_MSGRAPH_TENANT_ID (Docker environment variables)
tools.description: Enable OneDrive/SharePoint storage through a Microsoft Entra (Azure AD) application: client id and secret of the registered app, plus DRAWIO_MSGRAPH_TENANT_ID for single-tenant apps. Unset means OneDrive is disabled and hidden from the storage dialogs.
tools.notes: The ms365=0 URL parameter disables the separate Microsoft 365 integration used by the Teams/Office apps.

tools.name: DRAWIO_GITLAB_ID / DRAWIO_GITLAB_SECRET / DRAWIO_GITLAB_URL (Docker environment variables)
tools.description: Enable GitLab storage: DRAWIO_GITLAB_ID and DRAWIO_GITLAB_SECRET are the OAuth application credentials and DRAWIO_GITLAB_URL is the GitLab base URL without any path (https://gitlab.com or a self-hosted host). For a non-gitlab.com URL the entrypoint also writes Editor.enableCustomGitLabUrl = true into PostConfig.js, which the client needs to allow the instance.

parameters.name: DRAWIO_GITLAB_URL
parameters.description: Base URL only; /oauth/token and /oauth/authorize are appended automatically.

tools.notes: Adding a path to DRAWIO_GITLAB_URL breaks the OAuth flow. Per-session equivalents are the gitlab= and gitlab-id= URL parameters.

tools.name: jgraph/drawio Docker image (self-hosted web app)
tools.description: Official container that serves the draw.io web application (Tomcat) for private hosting: docker run -p 8080:8080 jgraph/drawio starts it on http://localhost:8080; docker-compose.yml passes every DRAWIO_* variable from a .env file. It includes the editor, viewer scripts, templates and stencils; cloud storage is disabled until OAuth variables are set, and a reverse proxy normally terminates TLS in front of it.

parameters.name: -p 8080:8080
parameters.description: Container HTTP port (8443 for HTTPS when a keystore is configured).

parameters.name: DRAWIO_*
parameters.description: Environment variables documented in this category.

parameters.name: GID 0
parameters.description: Container must run with group 0 for runtime configuration.

tools.example:
docker run -it --rm --name drawio -p 8080:8080 -p 8443:8443 jgraph/drawio
# then open http://localhost:8080/?offline=1&https=0
tools.notes: The separate jgraph/export-server image is end-of-life; the container now sets window.EXPORT_URL = null, so PDF export uses the browser print dialog and server-rendered PNG is hidden (browser-side PNG/SVG export still works).

tools.name: Image export service (draw-image-export2, POST /export)
tools.description: The server-side renderer behind File > Export as > PDF on app.diagrams.net and the 'Include a copy of my diagram' PNG option, implemented with Node, Puppeteer and headless Chrome (jgraph/draw-image-export2). It accepts GET or POST parameters: xml (diagram XML, URL-encoded) or xmldata (deflated+base64+URL-encoded) or url (remote file), format png|jpg|pdf, w/h (viewport), bg (background colour), border, scale, from/to/pageId/allPages (page selection), embedXml (embed the diagram in the PNG), base64 (encode the response), filename (Content-Disposition) and extras (JSON with layer names etc.). Self-hosters can run it with npm start and point EXPORT_URL at it.

parameters.name: xml / xmldata / url
parameters.description: Diagram source (xmldata takes precedence over xml).

parameters.name: embedXml / base64 / filename
parameters.description: PNG embedding, response encoding and download name.

tools.notes: The public endpoint is intended for the draw.io apps; for automation prefer the desktop CLI (drawio -x) or a headless container, which need no server. The Docker web image no longer bundles an export server.
